newsitem.title: USA: ITT adds hotels amid Hilton takeover fight.
newsitem.headline: ITT adds hotels amid Hilton takeover fight.

text.p: ITT Corp. moved forward Thursday with its effort to battle a hostile $6.5 billion bid from Hilton Hotels Corp., announcing plans to add 28 hotels to its core Sheraton business.
The move came one day after Hilton, which is seeking to take control of ITT in a proxy fight, filed a motion in a Nevada federal court to force ITT to hold its annual shareholders meeting in May.

The latest transactions call for ITT to take on management and franchise agreements for 27 hotels, as well as the acquisition of a hotel in Monterrey, Mexico, for $15 million. The deal includes 18 Four Points hotels in the United States, Canada and Israel, and 10 Sheraton hotels around the world.
It was the second major step taken by ITT since it earlier this month rejected Hilton's offer and said it may sell non-core assets to focus on hotel and casino operations.
ITT spokesman Jim Gallagher said the move was not directly linked to the Hilton offer, noting that some of the transactions had been under discussion since late last year.
Hilton, based in Beverly Hills, Calif., announced its unsolicited offer Jan. 27. The bid also calls for the assumption of about $4 billion in debt.
"We are moving ahead and making sure our core businesses are healthy and expanding. It is business as usual," Gallagher said, adding that similar agreeements were likely.

"We are going to continue to sign franchise properties and sign management contracts literally around the world and continue to increase what we think is already a very strong international lead in the hospitality industry," he said.
New York-based ITT took a first step to implement its anti-takeover plan earlier this month when it sold nearly half of its 5 percent stake in French telecommunications company Alcatel Alsthom.

ITT also is expected to sell its 50 percent stake in the Madison Square Garden properties, which include the famous arena and the Knicks professional basketball team and the Rangers professional hockey team.
Sources familiar with the matter said Thursday that Cablevision Systems Corp., which owns the other half of Madison Square Garden, has secured the upper hand to buy ITT's stake.

The sources, who did not want to be identified, said the two companies have quietly resolved a dispute over ownership rights. They have agreed that while Cablevision is not entitled to prevent another company from bidding, it has the right to compete with the best bid, they said.
The sources said it was not immediately clear if Cablevision would have to match the bid or exceed it. One source said he believed Cablevision would only have to top an offer by $1.

Major media companies also have lined up to bid. Although no formal offers have been submitted, interest has been expressed by News Corp. Ltd., General Electric Co., Westinghouse Electric Corp., Walt Disney Co. and Loews Corp., the sources said.
A Hilton spokesman said Thursday that ITT's addition of 28 hotels was not likely to prompt a change in his company's bid.
"I don't anticipate it would change the offer," Marc Grossman, Hilton's senior vice president-corporate affairs, said. "But obviously we don't know the financial details."
Depending on the quality of the 28 hotels, Hilton might welcome the deal, Grossman said.

Meanwhile, the court motion filed by Hilton cites ITT bylaws and case law as a legal basis for holding the shareholders meeting at its normal time. The suit was filed in U.S. District Court in Las Vegas.
ITT, which traditionally holds its yearly meeting in May, has not yet set a date for this year's session. It is permitted to schedule a meeting any time until mid-November.

ITT stock dipped 75 cents to $56.375 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. The stock had been trading at about $42 before Hilton announced its cash and stock offer valuing ITT at about $55 a share.
Industry experts have said the $55-per-share offer is low, and many expect Hilton to raise its bid.

In addition to building its Sheraton presence, ITT plans to focus on its Caesars casino operations. The company is in the middle of a major capital expansion project for its casino business and has said it anticipates accelerated earnings growth as the projects are completed.

ITT also is bidding on Italian telephone directory business SEAT SpA, which is valued at near $1.6 billion. ITT is considering selling its world telephone directories business as part of the plan to divest non-core assets.
